title: Graph Studio · Appearance loading to rendering

metadata.description: The complete Appearance pipeline: JSON defaults, style sources, validation, active state, geometry inputs, SVG properties, CSS layers and export.
metadata.relationshipSemantics: Directed data flow and control flow. Optional paths are labelled. Arrows do not imply that every operation executes in one synchronous sequence.
metadata.hierarchySemantics: Groups represent responsibility boundaries. Nested subgroups expose internal processes; containment is independent of ordinary relationships.

open.title: 01 · Open a graph
open.define: Prepare a complete document before replacing the current session.
open.details: Expand this group to follow its internal steps. Containment indicates ownership; arrows indicate data flow or control flow.

appearance.title: 03 · Resolve appearance
appearance.define: Resolve chart defaults, preferences and document-linked styles.
appearance.details: Expand this group to follow its internal steps. Containment indicates ownership; arrows indicate data flow or control flow.

layout.title: 04 · Compute layout
layout.define: Turn document and view inputs into geometry; review optional arrangement proposals.
layout.details: Expand this group to follow its internal steps. Containment indicates ownership; arrows indicate data flow or control flow.

canvas.title: 05 · Render and explore
canvas.define: Draw the visible graph and manage interaction without changing containment.
canvas.details: Expand this group to follow its internal steps. Containment indicates ownership; arrows indicate data flow or control flow.

output.title: 06 · Save and export
output.define: Preserve the editable document or capture the current visible view.
output.details: Expand this group to follow its internal steps. Containment indicates ownership; arrows indicate data flow or control flow.

layout-baseline.title: Stage construction
layout-baseline.define: Prepare the visible projection, measure content and run chart algorithms.
layout-baseline.details: Expand this group to follow its internal steps. Containment indicates ownership; arrows indicate data flow or control flow.

prepare-document.title: Prepare a document
prepare-document.define: Parse and normalize the graph; resolve its optional linked style.
prepare-document.details: Check document shape and references before replacing the session. An unavailable linked style produces a notice rather than preventing the graph from opening.

style-sources.title: Default construction
style-sources.define: Import field definitions and combine base defaults with chart overrides.
style-sources.details: Default construction is separate from selecting a preset or restoring a saved style.

style-controls.title: Appearance controls
style-controls.define: Edit Nodes, Edges and Canvas properties or their Schema values.
style-controls.details: Controls and Schema editing use the same appearance contract. Chart Schema describes graph fields; it does not own layout computation.

resolve-style.title: Validate style values
resolve-style.define: Validate field types, bounds, enums and the chart-specific style envelope.
resolve-style.details: documentDefinition uses styleDefinition for the selected chart; resolveDefinition enforces the contract. Invalid stored preferences fall back to defaults, invalid file imports leave active state unchanged, and invalid linked styles surface a notice.

style-state.title: Resolved chart style
style-state.define: Provide validated appearance values and independent style history.
style-state.details: The active per-chart style supplies two branches: geometry inputs for layout and display/CSS inputs for drawing. It also retains independent undo history. ChartStyle includes display options and optional Timeline settings beyond appearance.

measure-content.title: Measure text and boxes
measure-content.define: Resolve font metrics and the dimensions needed by layout.
measure-content.details: The main thread uses browser Canvas measurements when available. Workers and static consumers retain a deterministic fallback; some worker inputs carry measured sizes.

run-layout.title: Run chart algorithms
run-layout.define: Compute positions and routes for the selected chart family.
run-layout.details: Node-link, Nested, Timeline, Sankey and Spatial use separate pipelines. Nested layout arranges inner scopes before their parents. Candidate searches use workers where implemented.

stage-data.title: Build stage data
stage-data.define: Assemble positioned nodes, paths, labels and canvas bounds.
stage-data.details: Stage geometry is derived from the document and view. It is not a replacement for the editable graph document.

render-svg.title: Render the SVG stage
render-svg.define: Render nodes, edges, group frames and chart backdrops.
render-svg.details: The main canvas and preview canvases reuse stage renderers. SVG style sources are also used by exports.

export-svg.title: Export current SVG
export-svg.define: Capture the current visible projection as an SVG file.
export-svg.details: Collapsed descendants are not individually drawn in the exported view. The editable graph JSON still preserves those descendants.

export-html.title: Export interactive HTML
export-html.define: Capture graph and SVG together for the standalone viewer.
export-html.details: The export snapshots the document and SVG before asynchronously loading the HTML exporter. The offline viewer cannot expand descendants omitted from the captured projection.

persist-session.title: Persist browser state
persist-session.define: Remember preferences, recent locations and AI session state.
persist-session.details: Browser state supports returning to work. It is separate from explicitly saving graph JSON to a source file or downloading a copy.

style-loading.title: Style loading and validation
style-loading.define: Expand this group to inspect the appearance pipeline.
style-loading.details: Containment indicates responsibility. Labelled arrows show configuration, state changes and rendering inputs.

style-session.title: Active style and history
style-session.define: Expand this group to inspect the appearance pipeline.
style-session.details: Containment indicates responsibility. Labelled arrows show configuration, state changes and rendering inputs.

style-geometry.title: Appearance layout inputs
style-geometry.define: Expand this group to inspect the appearance pipeline.
style-geometry.details: Containment indicates responsibility. Labelled arrows show configuration, state changes and rendering inputs.

style-rendering.title: Appearance SVG rendering
style-rendering.define: Expand this group to inspect the appearance pipeline.
style-rendering.details: Containment indicates responsibility. Labelled arrows show configuration, state changes and rendering inputs.

field-json.title: Field definition JSON
field-json.define: Define fields, defaults, enums, bounds and UI metadata.
field-json.details: Contains appearance, timeline and display-option definitions. This is runtime configuration, not the rendered stylesheet.

definition-import.title: Import definitions
definition-import.define: Import JSON and expose the three field-definition objects.
definition-import.details: ES module imports load bundled JSON. The Vite compatibility plugin strips JSON import attributes for its older esbuild; it does not generate configuration.

chart-default-json.title: Chart override JSON
chart-default-json.define: Supply default overrides for each chart type.
chart-default-json.details: These values specialize base defaults. Presets are separate complete snapshots and are not automatically layered onto defaults.

construct-style.title: Compose chart defaults
construct-style.define: Build styleDefinition and apply chart-specific default overrides.
construct-style.details: resolveDefinition first supplies base values. mergeDefinitionValues applies chart overrides, and styleDefinition assigns the resulting leaf defaults. defaultChartStyle resolves the complete style.

default-style.title: Default ChartStyle
default-style.define: Provide appearance, display options and optional Timeline settings.
default-style.details: getDefaultChartStyle supplies initialization and reset. ChartStyle includes showNodeDetail, hideNodeBorders and alignNodeWidthsToMax outside appearance; Timeline also has style.timeline.

browser-style.title: Restore browser preferences
browser-style.define: Read graph-studio:page-preferences and validate each saved chart style.
browser-style.details: Valid saved styles replace defaults for their chart type. Missing or invalid saved styles fall back to that chart default. Storage failure also falls back to defaults.

preset-style.title: Preset JSON snapshots
preset-style.define: Load and validate complete preset documents; clone a selected preset.
preset-style.details: Preset identity and document validation happen at module loading. Selecting a preset commits its cloned style; selecting Reset uses chart defaults instead.

imported-style.title: Import a style file
imported-style.define: Read a selected JSON file and check its chart type and envelope.
imported-style.details: importAppearanceFile parses the document before commitStyle. Invalid imports report an error and do not commit the imported values.

linked-style.title: Resolve metadata.style
linked-style.define: Resolve the document-relative style path within the opened workspace.
linked-style.details: Only granted workspace files are read. A valid style is attached to the prepared document; unavailable or invalid linked styles produce a notice without preventing graph opening.

resolved-document.title: Validated style document
resolved-document.define: Produce a complete graph-studio-style envelope and its style member.
resolved-document.details: parseStyleDocument calls resolveDefinition(documentDefinition(chartType), value). parseChartStyleFile returns the style member. Field validation and envelope validation share the same contract.

activate-style.title: Activate a chart style
activate-style.define: Initialize from preferences, or replace with the newly opened document style.
activate-style.details: State is indexed by chart type. A valid linked style takes effect on document generation change. Leaving a linked-style document restores the stored user preference. Presets and edits subsequently update the active style.

ui-bindings.title: Bind controls to Schema
ui-bindings.define: Resolve field paths, visibility, supported charts and reset values.
ui-bindings.details: Ordinary controls bind to field definitions. The Schema editor uses the same update contract; it does not implement a separate validation pipeline.

validate-edit.title: Validate an atomic edit
validate-edit.define: Apply changes and dependent resets, then validate the complete style document.
validate-edit.details: updateAppearanceSchemaValues edits a clone, checks writable supported paths, applies declared reset dependencies and parses the entire result. Custom CSS commands also use the appearance resolver.

commit-style.title: Commit style and history
commit-style.define: Record appearance changes with before and after values.
commit-style.details: commitStyle also carries display options and Timeline settings. Slider adjustments can be grouped; style undo and redo remain separate from graph-edit history.

style-undo.title: Undo or redo appearance
style-undo.define: Restore style history and synchronize Timeline settings where applicable.
style-undo.details: Changing a chart style does not rewrite ordinary graph nodes or edges. Document layout metadata has a separate owner.

persist-style.title: Save reusable preferences
persist-style.define: Persist chart styles while excluding document-linked overrides.
persist-style.details: For a linked-style document, persistence retains the stored user chart preference. Timeline typeColors and pins are cleared and locked is false in reusable preferences. Browser persistence does not overwrite the linked style file.

extract-geometry.title: Extract StageAppearance
extract-geometry.define: Select dimensions, spacing, font roles, palette and relevant display flags.
extract-geometry.details: getStageAppearance extracts canvas, nodes, edges, typography and detail/date/axis/track fonts. Compound display flags include group stats and title wrapping. Palette is still included, so color changes are not universally render-only.

font-readiness.title: Track font readiness
font-readiness.define: Invalidate measurements when browser fonts become available.
font-readiness.details: The font metrics key participates in StageAppearance. Registered font tokens affect both measurement and SVG text; arbitrary custom CSS font changes do not participate in geometry measurement.

geometry-cache.title: Memoize and debounce
geometry-cache.define: Compare serialized geometry inputs and settle rapid changes.
geometry-cache.details: JSON.stringify creates the geometry comparison key; useMemo preserves equivalent inputs. useDebouncedValue settles changes with a default 150 ms delay before expensive layout work.

layout-options.title: Supply layout options
layout-options.define: Pass detail visibility, width alignment and chart-specific settings.
layout-options.details: showNodeDetail and alignNodeWidthsToMax also affect layout. Nested showEdgeLabels participates separately in compound layout input. Timeline settings have a separate debounced path.

svg-vars.title: Map SVG CSS variables
svg-vars.define: Convert cssVars and derived effects into root SVG style properties.
svg-vars.details: appearanceToStageStyle derives shadows, dot visibility, content shift, edge-label color fallback and Sankey opacity. The resulting object is assigned to the root svg style.

svg-properties.title: Apply component properties
svg-properties.define: Pass display flags, colors and density behavior to SVG components.
svg-properties.details: Not every property becomes CSS: group fills and borders, edge-label visibility, marker style and dense-shadow attributes are consumed by React components. hideNodeBorders comes from ChartStyle outside appearance.

svg-defs.title: Build GraphDefs
svg-defs.define: Embed stylesheets and arrow markers in the SVG.
svg-defs.details: GraphDefs declares graph-base, graph-theme and graph-custom layers, then embeds their CSS in a style element inside defs. Marker geometry also depends on appearance.

css-base.title: graph-base layer
css-base.define: Combine structural graph CSS and default graph CSS.
css-base.details: GraphDefs combines GRAPH_BASE_CSS with DEFAULT_GRAPH_CSS in the base layer.

css-theme.title: graph-theme layer
css-theme.define: Apply built-in effects and Timeline rules.
css-theme.details: GraphDefs combines GRAPH_EFFECTS_CSS and TIMELINE_CSS in the theme layer.

css-custom.title: graph-custom layer
css-custom.define: Embed validated appearance.css in the final named layer.
css-custom.details: For normal layered declarations the custom layer follows theme and base. Inline data styling still has its own cascade priority; custom CSS is not an unconditional override of every SVG property.

svg-compose.title: Compose SVG elements
svg-compose.define: Combine stage geometry, style properties and embedded definitions.
svg-compose.details: GraphNode, GraphEdge, group components and chart-specific renderers consume stage data and appearance. The main canvas and preview canvases reuse these rendering components.
